body:
## Problem

The system is a reactive oracle — it reports what prices are, not what they will be. DeFi protocols that rely on this data cannot anticipate price movements, cannot hedge against predicted volatility, and cannot optimize execution timing. The system has months of accumulated historical price data that is being used only for current-value queries, not for prediction.

## Requirements

- **Production ML pipeline** — Build an end-to-end ML pipeline with: feature engineering (technical indicators: moving averages, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, volatility, volume profile, cross-source spread), model training (LSTM, XGBoost, ARIMA, and a stacked ensemble), model versioning (MLflow or DVC), hyperparameter optimization (Optuna), and online inference with sub-100ms p99 latency.
- **Real-time online inference** — Every 30-second aggregation cycle triggers inference for each asset. The inference must complete in <50ms per asset (to stay within the aggregation window). Models are loaded into memory at service startup and hot-reloaded when a new model version is deployed.
- **A/B model comparison in production** — Run two (or more) prediction models side by side on the same input. Compare predicted vs actual prices, track MAPE, RMSE, and directional accuracy. Expose comparison dashboard in Grafana. Automatically promote the better-performing model.
- **Drift detection and automated retraining** — Monitor feature drift (distribution of input features) and concept drift (prediction accuracy over time). When drift exceeds configurable thresholds, trigger automated retraining pipeline: fetch new training data, run hyperparameter search, train candidate models, evaluate against holdout, and deploy if improved. All automated, gated by accuracy guardrails.
- **Prediction confidence and uncertainty quantification** — Every prediction includes: point estimate, prediction interval (80%/95%), confidence score based on model agreement, and source of uncertainty (aleatory vs epistemic). Low-confidence predictions (<60%) are not exposed to API consumers but are logged for analysis.
- **Risk-aware aggregation integration** — The aggregator can optionally use predictions to: detect anomalous oracle submissions (predictor says $50k but source submits $200k), weight sources by their recent predictive accuracy, or provide "expected correction" metadata alongside each price.
- **API exposure** — Endpoints: `GET /v1/predictions/:asset` (current prediction), `GET /v1/predictions/:asset/history` (past predictions vs actuals), `GET /v1/models` (active model metadata, accuracy metrics).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ML pipeline with feature engineering, training, versioning, hyperparameter optimization
- [ ] Online inference <50ms per asset at p99
- [ ] A/B model comparison in production with automated promotion
- [ ] Drift detection with automated retraining pipeline (gated by accuracy guardrails)
- [ ] Prediction intervals and confidence scores for every prediction
- [ ] Aggregator integration: anomaly detection and source weighting by predictive accuracy
- [ ] 3 API endpoints for predictions, history, and model metadata
- [ ] Prometheus metrics for prediction accuracy, inference latency, drift scores
- [ ] Grafana dashboard showing model comparison, drift, accuracy trends
title: Production ML pipeline for price prediction with A/B model comparison, drift detection, and uncertainty quantification
